newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks close weaker but evade Dow drop.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks close weaker but evade Dow drop.

text.p: CHANGE CHANGE

* Toronto stocks closed softer on Friday, but managed to avoid Wall Street tumble. * Profit-taking, double-witching blamed for weakness. * 89 million shares traded worth C$1.4 billion.
Toronto stocks ended weaker in moderate trading on Friday amid profit-taking and double-witching, but managed to avoid Wall Street's steep drop.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index slid 29.27 points to 6247.38. The Dow Jones Industrial Average shed 139 points to close at 7195.

"People going into a weekend, whether long or short, want to take profits," said Fred Ketchen, director of trading at ScotiaMcLeod. Canadian markets will be closed on Monday for the Victoria Day holiday.
Ketchen said that double witching, the expiration of options and futures, added to volatility in both markets.
In Toronto, heavyweight golds lost 1.6 percent on weak bullion prices. "We can't get any long-term or consistent news out of the gold sector," Ketchen said.
All of Toronto's 14 sub-indices weakened except for retail and utilities. Gold stocks were the top losers, followed by real estate, banks, media and transportation.
Declining stocks outpaced advances 380 to 328, while 262 issues were flat.
Canada's largest stock market ended the week nearly flat from Monday's opening level of 6239.04 points.
--- HOT STOCKS ---
* Shares in gold prospector Golden Rule Resources Ltd fell 3.46, or nearly 47 percent, to close at 3.94 on 2.6 million shares.

The company has hired a consultant to review its gold joint venture in Ghana after check assay reports for the Ghana Minerals Commission suggested Golden Rule's assay results for the site were overstated.
* Pure Gold Resources Inc lost 0.09 to close at 0.41 on 7.0 million shares after the release of drill results from its diamond joint venture in Alberta.
